model_annotation: Figure 4 illustrates the number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial, as part of a user study to assess the tool's effectiveness. The bar chart displays the frequency of positive feedback for six distinct evaluation criteria, which are listed along the horizontal axis: "retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)", "concise summaries and explanations", "clarity of the interface", "overall usability", "output quality", and "satisfaction with fact-checking". The vertical axis represents the number of participants, with a scale ranging from 0 to 6. The data shows that the highest number of participants (5) found the "retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)" to be beneficial. The "concise summaries and explanations" and "clarity of the interface" were each highlighted by 4 participants. The "overall usability" and "output quality" were each selected by 3 participants. The "satisfaction with fact-checking" criterion received the lowest number of mentions, with only 2 participants identifying it as beneficial. The bars are arranged in descending order of frequency, with the tallest bar corresponding to "retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)".
